metadata.purpose: Operational project memory for AI-agent-led development.
metadata.architecture: single-process telegram bot plus scraper plus scheduler plus digest delivery

entity.name: User
entity.summary: Telegram user identity, top-level preferences, and owner scope for per-user subscription limits.

entity.name: Subscription
entity.summary: Named digest configuration owned by one user, including editable AI filter and summary task prompts; can be created manually or from static global channel presets up to the configured per-user limit, and is shown in the subscription list with a next-digest countdown when enabled.

entity.name: SubscriptionChannel
entity.summary: Join entity between subscription and channel with subscribed_at baseline.

entity.name: DigestDelivery
entity.summary: Per-subscription processed-post record, delivered/skipped status, skip reason, and summary metadata snapshot.

entity.name: DigestProcessingLog
entity.summary: Completed per-subscription processing-run totals for found, filtered, and included posts, including zero-result runs.

entity.name: OnDemandDigest
entity.summary: Claimed or completed manual digest keyed by subscription, normalized period, and effective prompt fingerprint; persists rendered Telegram-safe messages for idempotent resend.

entity.name: ChatMessage
entity.summary: Persisted chat history for assistant context, visible system confirmations, and recent digest references.

entity.name: LlmUsage
entity.summary: Non-sensitive OpenRouter completion attempt telemetry: model, use case, status, available usage/cost fields, error class text, and timestamp without prompts or outputs.

entity.name: KnowledgeDocument
entity.summary: One fixed-schema semantic enrichment record for a canonical Post; synthetic metadata is not a citation source.

entity.name: KnowledgeRepresentation
entity.summary: Versioned summary, full, or original-text chunk retrieval representation linked to one parent Post.

entity.name: KnowledgeChannel, KnowledgeChannelRequest, KnowledgeImport, KnowledgeQuery, KnowledgeFeedback
entity.summary: Administrator-moderated public catalog with a hash-refreshed metadata-only description, temporary export audit trail with content-free enrichment/embedding/total cost totals, content-free per-stage search audit, and fixed-code feedback.

modules.module: Application bootstrap; owns shared process services such as OpenRouter model pool and AssistantMemoryService.

Optional FastAPI/Uvicorn read-only dashboard with PBKDF2 environment login, signed session, responsive analytics page including latest manually-labelled RAG retrieval metrics, and in-memory login retry bound.
Telegram command and callback routing, including subscription-list buttons with next-digest countdown labels and a subscription processing-log action for the last 24 hours.

User and subscription operations, product-limit enforcement for subscription/channel counts, plus bot-facing subscription label/list formatting with visible limit counters and user-scoped processing-log aggregates.
Channel page scraping orchestration, including bounded pagination to a requested period boundary.
Telegram page to ParsedPost conversion.

Due-checking, cascade batch summary filtering/synthesis, formatting, summary fallback, delivery/skipped persistence, completed processing-run logging including zero-result runs, and candidate-prompt rendering for isolated replay.
Periodic scraping, digest, and LLM model refresh jobs.

OpenRouter chat, embeddings, bounded rerank, model-list, structured-output request parameters, HTTP error body previews, tool-probe adapter, and separately scheduled bounded content-free usage telemetry callback. The production API key has external PII-redaction and prompt-injection flag guardrails.

Minimal OpenAI-compatible async client for the direct DeepSeek API (deepseek-v4-flash), used only for bounded knowledge work (grounded RAG answers when the answer_direct_enabled flag is on, and the offline semantic claim judge). It records content-free usage telemetry (knowledge_answer_direct / knowledge_answer_judge) and never stores prompt or response content.

Content-free semantic claim judge for offline evaluation: DeepSeek-backed pairwise equivalence between a generated claim and a reviewed claim using only claim text and canonical post ids; returns True/False/None, aggregates verdicts only, and is versioned by a non-secret judge_version setting.

Hourly free-model refresh with persistent quality exclusions, DeepSeek V4 Flash paid emergency fallback, bounded assistant tool-support probing, in-memory runtime order, and per-use-case health backoff.
Channel persistence and lifecycle state.
Post upsert and retrieval.
Subscription and membership persistence.
Delivery dedup and summary metadata persistence, completed processing-run aggregate storage/querying, plus read-only subscription-period selection for prompt replay and on-demand rendering.
Atomic on-demand digest cache claim, completion, and retrieval.

LLM-first natural-language control orchestration over authorized tools, plus a deterministic public-RAG router that uses a fresh trusted catalog snapshot, never silently widens catalog scope, and bypasses mem0 for catalog-routing/search turns.
Internal MCP-like product tools scoped to the current Telegram user, including read-only digest prompt replay, processing-log aggregates, and idempotent on-demand digest generation.
Cron validation, 15-minute minimum interval enforcement, cron due checks, next-digest timestamp calculation, and safe localized labels for daily and interval schedules.
Independent mem0-backed semantic memory layer around assistant turns; local Qdrant/history files live under .data/mem0.
Shared Telegram HTML instructions and sanitizer for assistant replies and digest text.

Authorized catalog moderation, durable canonical-post import, hash-refreshed metadata-only descriptions, fixed-schema enrichment, bounded retries, parent-scoped hybrid retrieval, structured claim answers with inline canonical citations, and canary-only reranking with provider/cost fallback. When answer_direct_enabled is set, interactive grounded answers run through the direct DeepSeek API (deepseek-v4-flash) instead of OpenRouter, with the OpenRouter chain retained as fallback. Matching graph/vector, code-navigation, and documentation questions receive small fixed retrieval facets before parent fusion; their selected facet sources are mandatory citations in the structured answer contract. It commits a content-free retrieval trace before the unbounded interactive answer call, so an incomplete query remains observable during the BL-24 measurement phase. The offline evaluator can atomically checkpoint only numeric aggregates and resume one exact dataset/configuration after a provider interruption.

Offline labelled-dataset evaluation with dev/eval split filtering, negative-case abstention/false-attribution metrics measured by the generated answer (empty vs non-empty claims) rather than raw retrieval emptiness, source sufficiency plus claim-coverage sufficiency, citation precision/recall/F1 and thesis-to-link placement, deterministic claim heuristics and an optional content-free DeepSeek semantic claim judge, content-free atomic checkpoints, and operator flags --split, --judge, --print-samples, --limit, --checkpoint, --rerank-limit, --direct, --concurrency. The case loop is parallelized with a bounded semaphore (concurrency up to 10); each case uses its own isolated session and external provider calls (embed/rerank/answer/judge) are concurrent-safe, while Qdrant client initialization is guarded by a thread lock.

Content-free DeepSeek semantic claim judge plus operator-only calibration tooling: the judge compares a generated claim against a reviewed claim by coverage of essential aspects (central assertion plus negations, limitations, scope, mappings) and is calibrated against a fixed operator-labelled pair set (v6 prompt, agreement 17/19 = 0.895); judge_prompt_score scores a prompt against a fixed labelled file without regenerating answers.
Paragraph-aware representations, isolated local Qdrant vector access, parent collapse/RRF, context reconstruction, and original Telegram permalink rendering.
Chat history persistence and recent digest retrieval.

Docker runtime starts PostgreSQL and the app unless explicitly stopped; the app waits for the database healthcheck, mounts config.toml and manually labelled evaluation datasets read-only, and persists local assistant memory in ./.data at /app/.data.

flow.name: User onboarding and preferences
flow.summary: Registers user, shows an editable Telegram-safe HTML /start guide without a duplicated external title, positions Channel Scanner as an AI service for selected public text Telegram channels, focus management, flexible filtering, scheduled digests, and future knowledge-base use, picks language, stores timezone and language, and can run in one allowlisted E2E chat for black-box verification.

flow.name: Subscription management
flow.summary: Create manually or from static global channel presets up to the configured per-user subscription limit, rename, configure, enable, disable, and delete named subscriptions; the subscription list shows enabled subscriptions with a short next-digest countdown and visible subscription/channel limit counters, while each subscription exposes found/filtered/included processing totals for the last 24 hours; deletion removes subscription-scoped channel links and processing state before deleting the subscription row.

flow.name: Channel membership management
flow.summary: Validates public usernames, adds shared channels manually or from presets up to the configured per-subscription channel limit, removes channel membership per subscription.

flow.name: Scheduled scraping
flow.summary: Iterates active channels, fetches pages, parses posts, stores new posts, marks channel state.

flow.name: Scheduled digest delivery
flow.summary: Selects due subscriptions, finds unprocessed posts, renders digests, sends Telegram messages, stores delivered and skipped processing state, and persists found/filtered/included processing totals after each completed run, including zero-result runs.

flow.name: On-demand digest delivery
flow.summary: Resolves a user-owned named subscription and a timezone-aware period, claims an idempotent cache key, paginates its channels to the interval start while retaining at most 100 matching posts per channel, stores posts idempotently, renders and sends normal digest messages as the turn's only visible output, and caches them for exact resend without changing DigestDelivery, DigestProcessingLog, or last_digest_at.

flow.name: LLM summary generation
flow.summary: Uses an hourly refreshed OpenRouter free-model pool, excluding permanently disqualified models, followed by DeepSeek V4 Flash as a paid emergency fallback for empty-post pre-skip plus structured JSON schema filter-then-synthesize batch summaries. The production OpenRouter API key externally redacts configured PII and flags prompt-injection matches; it does not apply thematic political/crime moderation. The flow supports editable task-only AI filter prompts while app-owned memory/preference handling remains mandatory, supports editable summary prompts with an approved brief default, exposes candidate prompt overrides for read-only replay, enforces target-language/plain-field prompt rules, strips accidental leading topic bullets before rendering source-linked topic bullets, retries the next model on invalid JSON, and falls back safely to 200-character mode on failure or empty model output.

flow.name: Natural-language bot control
flow.summary: Uses an hourly refreshed OpenRouter free-model assistant pool with DeepSeek V4 Flash as the paid emergency fallback and cached tool-support probes, stops inline probing once a confirmed assistant model is available, and uses internal tools to inspect and mutate bot product state including AI filter/summary prompts and read-only processing-log aggregates; for dissatisfaction with digest output, it first asks for a missing desired result, then prioritizes replaying a persisted subscription period through candidate prompts without sending or persisting state before proposing or mutating prompts. Explicit confirmation remains required before prompt mutation. The assistant prompt includes current product limits and tool executions are capped per turn; explains capabilities/how-to-use questions in simple language, shows Telegram typing feedback while the turn runs, then emits deterministic localized Telegram-safe HTML confirmations with bold subscription names.

flow.name: Assistant semantic memory
flow.summary: Retrieves and updates mem0 semantic memories independently from the assistant; memory mutation tools are not exposed to the model. Compose mounts ./.data to /app/.data so local Qdrant/history state survives app recreates. The app creates one shared process-local memory service for scheduler digest filtering and bot assistant turns.

flow.name: Read-only admin dashboard
flow.entrypoints: HTTPS csd.ai-research.arha.digital through Caddy; internal FastAPI server
flow.summary: Uses an environment-configured PBKDF2 password hash and signed session to show responsive 24-hour, 7-day, all-time from the first stored event, or custom UTC aggregate views with mobile-safe dd.mm chart axes. It reads product counts, activity, delivery/processing outcomes, current channel errors, LLM telemetry, and content-free RAG configuration/evaluation aggregates without exposing allowlists, prompts, queries, posts, or answers or mutating product state.

flow.name: Public-channel knowledge search
flow.summary: The assistant loads READY catalog names, metadata-only descriptions, counts, and sync timestamps as trusted context. It lists that snapshot without a tool round; explicit @username searches one channel, while channel-free questions propose one confirmed match or a choice of up to three and never widen scope silently. RAG routing/search bypasses mem0. Grounded answers contain validated structured claims with inline one-to-five original Telegram links; descriptions and retrieval representations are not evidence. Matching fixed retrieval facets require their selected sources to be cited. During BL-24 measurement vector retrieval, reranking, and answer generation have no configured interactive time limit; benchmark selection sets the canary to rerank the maximum 20 scope-authorized parents.

flow.name: Knowledge catalog moderation and import
flow.entrypoints: Assistant requestKnowledgeChannel tool, Telegram administrator callbacks and JSON document upload
flow.summary: Users create pending public-channel requests. Only configured Telegram administrators approve/reject and upload bounded official JSON exports; imports persist canonical posts before optional enrichment/indexing. Failed enrichment or vectorization retains bounded retry/error state for the four-hour job, and raw export JSON is never stored in PostgreSQL.

invariant.name: No duplicate delivery per subscription/post
invariant.summary: The same post must not be delivered or skipped twice for the same subscription; any DigestDelivery status removes it from pending selection.

invariant.name: No duplicate persisted post per channel/post_id
invariant.summary: Re-scraping must be idempotent for existing Telegram posts.

invariant.name: No historical posts before subscribed_at
invariant.summary: Posts published before a subscription added the channel must not appear in future digests for that subscription.

invariant.name: Timezone and frequency control due delivery
invariant.summary: Daily and hourly digests plus subscription-list countdown labels must respect user timezone, notification cron, and legacy subscription frequency fallback.

invariant.name: Summary failures must not block delivery
invariant.summary: If free summary model refresh, structured filter/synthesis JSON, model calls, empty model output, or model health selection fail, the bot must retry usable models including the final DeepSeek V4 Flash paid emergency fallback when possible and still send a short digest for non-empty posts using normal digest grouping; empty extracted posts are skipped before LLM calls.

invariant.name: Reply context never replaces current post body
invariant.summary: Scraped reply posts must store and summarize the current post text, excluding replied-to/quoted Telegram context from digest rendering and LLM input.

invariant.name: Visible bot output must remain Telegram-safe HTML
invariant.summary: Rendered digest and assistant output must keep allowed tags and valid links without raw Markdown or broken Telegram formatting; batch topic summaries are rendered with one app-owned bullet marker even if a model returns a leading bullet; assistant mutation confirmations must localize RU/EN text and bold subscription names with escaped Telegram HTML.

invariant.name: Channel membership is per subscription, not global per user
invariant.summary: Each named subscription has its own channel list and delivery scope.

invariant.name: Notification cron interval is bounded
invariant.summary: Assistant-provided notification cron expressions must not fire more often than every 15 minutes; valid interval schedules such as every 3 hours must render in tools and bot screens without crashing.

invariant.name: Assistant mutations go through authorized tools
invariant.summary: The assistant can mutate product state only through user-scoped product tools, never raw repositories or database sessions; assistant model selection must prefer models with confirmed tool support.

invariant.name: Assistant memory is not tool-managed by the model
invariant.summary: mem0 memory retrieval/extraction is performed by an independent layer; the assistant does not receive save/delete memory tools.

invariant.name: Local mem0 state persists outside the container
invariant.summary: When local mem0 storage is enabled, Qdrant and history files must stay under the host-mounted .data path, be excluded from git and Docker build context, and be accessed by only one process-local memory service to avoid Qdrant local lock conflicts.

invariant.name: Editable filter prompts cannot override app guardrails
invariant.summary: User-editable AI filter prompts are limited to the filter Task. JSON schema output, dynamic post serialization, and explicit memory/preference handling are app-owned prompt sections outside editable text.

invariant.name: Product limits are enforced at mutation boundaries
invariant.summary: Configured limits cap assistant tool executions per turn, subscriptions per user, and channels per subscription for both UI and natural-language assistant mutation paths; visible subscription lists and assistant instructions expose those limits to users/LLM.

invariant.name: Prompt replay is isolated from delivery state
invariant.summary: Prompt replay may read persisted posts within a user-owned subscription, its channel subscribed_at baseline, and a selected interval, but must not scrape, send Telegram messages, create DigestDelivery or ChatMessage rows, or update last_digest_at.

invariant.name: Processing logs are completed and user-scoped
invariant.summary: Only a successful completed subscription run may persist found/filtered/included totals, including zero-result runs; menu and assistant reads must stay within the current user's subscription and never mutate delivery state.

invariant.name: On-demand digest is cached and isolated
invariant.summary: The same user-owned subscription, normalized [start, end) period, and effective filter/summary prompts must reuse one rendered result without repeating scraping or LLM generation; manual delivery must not create scheduled delivery or processing-log state or update last_digest_at, and no assistant reply may repeat or summarize tool-rendered digest text in the same turn.

invariant.name: Admin dashboard is authenticated and read-only
invariant.summary: Dashboard routes require the configured password-hash login and signed session; its API reads aggregates only and cannot invoke bot, subscription, channel, or delivery mutation operations.

invariant.name: LLM telemetry is non-blocking and content-free
invariant.summary: Telemetry stores only model, use case, status, available tokens/cost, error class text, and timestamp. It is scheduled separately with a bounded write attempt; its delay or failure must not hold up normal model fallback, digest delivery, or assistant turns.

invariant.name: External OpenRouter input guardrails have a narrow scope
invariant.summary: The production API key redacts configured PII before provider forwarding and records prompt-injection matches in flag mode. It does not block political, criminal, or true-crime subject matter, does not scan model output, and must not be switched to block mode until the client treats a guardrail 403 as terminal.

invariant.name: Knowledge citations are canonical parent posts
invariant.summary: Post.content is stored once as the source of truth. Summary cards, full embeddings, chunks, vector payloads, and LLM outputs can retrieve or rank but never become user-visible citations.

invariant.name: Public catalog discovery resolves one explicit safe scope
invariant.summary: A channel-free question may rank metadata-only READY catalog entries, but cannot search posts until the user confirms a clear match or chooses one channel. The catalog snapshot, descriptions, memories, and chat history are never answer evidence.

invariant.name: Knowledge scope and baseline apply before parent sources
invariant.summary: Subscription search enforces owner, linked channels, and subscribed_at on parent Post records before lexical/vector candidates can become sources; catalog history requires an explicit catalog-channel scope.

invariant.name: Knowledge fallback and Qdrant isolation
invariant.summary: Knowledge enrichment, catalog descriptions, and grounded interactive answers call their configured direct DeepSeek V4 Flash model and record content-free telemetry. Failed enrichment and vectorization retain bounded attempts plus content-free errors for later automatic retry; exhausted failures preserve normal lexical search. The one process-local knowledge Qdrant client uses .data/knowledge/qdrant and never shares mem0's path or collection.

invariant.name: Knowledge imports never create a digest backlog
invariant.summary: Every post from an administrator JSON catalog backfill receives a subscription-scoped skipped delivery record with reason knowledge_import_backfill for existing channel memberships. This keeps canonical/RAG persistence separate from normal scraper-driven digest eligibility.

invariant.name: Candidate RAG is canary-only and reversibly safe
invariant.summary: The BL-21 candidate is off by default for arbitrary deployments and is selected only when both the config flag and explicit Telegram allowlist match. This production configuration permanently selects only the dedicated E2E tester bot. It may send at most 20 scope-authorized canonical public posts to the reranker; missing credentials, provider errors, invalid results, unavailable cost, or configured cost-cap retain baseline ranking. During the BL-24 measurement phase, an interactive provider wait is deliberately not cut short by a configured timeout.

invariant.name: RAG rollout evidence is content-free
invariant.summary: RAG configuration snapshots, query telemetry, evaluation records, API payloads, and dashboard views contain identifiers and aggregate metrics only; they must not expose user IDs, allowlists, raw questions, posts, answers, or prompt text.
